## 🎓 Today's lesson: Non-Tariff Barriers
A **tariff** is a direct tax placed on goods arriving from another country, such as a 10% duty on imported steel. A **non-tariff barrier (NTB)** is a regulation, rule, or administrative obstacle that makes importing goods difficult without charging an explicit tax. 

Common examples include arbitrary safety certification delays, complex labeling requirements, quotas, or prolonged customs inspections. While tariffs are visible and easy to measure, non-tariff barriers are harder to challenge because governments often disguise them as standard domestic regulations. When Indian officials state that non-tariff barriers are the largest hurdle in trading with China, they mean that administrative hurdles—not formal tax rates—are blocking Indian medicines and IT services from entering the Chinese market. [[The Hindu]](https://www.thehindu.com/business/Economy/non-tariff-barriers-are-biggest-hurdle-in-india-china-trade-says-nirmala-sitharaman/article71591327.ece) [[The Economic Times]](https://news.google.?oc=5)
